text_blocks.snippet: Hypertension treatment options combine lifestyle changes and prescription medications to lower blood pressure below 130/80 mm Hg.

list.snippet: Dietary changes: Follow the DASH diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy while limiting sodium to under 1,500–2,000 mg per day.
Regular exercise: Get at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity per week.
Weight management: Lose excess body weight to reduce strain on the heart.
Habit adjustments: Limit alcohol intake, avoid tobacco products, and get 7 to 9 hours of sleep nightly.

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors often prescribe a combination of two or more medications, especially for Stage 2 hypertension. National Institutes of Health (NIH) | (.gov) +1

list.snippet: Angiotensin Receptor Blockers (ARBs): Relax blood vessels and protect the kidneys; frequently prescribed first (e.g., losartan).
ACE Inhibitors: Keep blood vessels from narrowing, though they may cause a dry cough in some patients (e.g., lisinopril).
Calcium Channel Blockers: Relax heart and blood vessel muscle cells to widen arteries (e.g., amlodipine).
Thiazide Diuretics: Water pills that remove extra sodium and fluid (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide).
